title: Google's AI Chip in Orbit Writes Poems
description: Google's Suncatcher prototype, built by Planet Labs, is online in orbit with four TPUs, only one of which runs at a time and for about twenty minutes. It runs the Gemma 4 model on test prompts while engineers check radiation and thermal effects; two more satellites are planned for 2027.

beats.vo: Google put an A I chip in orbit. Its first job: write a haiku.

beats.text: One of four chips runs at a time
beats.vo: The prototype carries four T P U chips, but only one runs at a time, for about twenty minutes. It's a test of Gemma four. But here's the catch: radiation can silently flip bits, so engineers are checking that now.
Think data centers must stay on Earth? Send this to the friend who loves space tech and ask what they think.

caption:
Google put an AI chip in orbit. Its first job: write a haiku. 🛰️
The Suncatcher prototype, built with Planet Labs, carries four TPUs but runs one at a time, about 20 minutes per run. It's testing Gemma 4 while engineers check radiation and heat effects.
The catch: this is a long-term moonshot. Two more satellites are planned for 2027.
Would you trust an AI chip in space? Comment your answer.
